analysis.title: GS Blekos - Marketcolour + Midterms Replay Earnings 5 Nov 2026
key_insights: US equities rallied after the midterms with lower oil and falling yields: SPX +158bps to 7688, NDX +91bps to 28,437, RTY +158bps to 2856. 8 of 11 sectors rose (Discretionary +5.09%, Communications +4.59%, Energy -4.75%).
Within AI infrastructure, owners of compute gained and builders and suppliers fell: hyperscalers +3.5%, neoclouds -7%, semis -2.5%, power -6%.
Rate-sensitive and lower-quality pockets outperformed: homebuilders (GSXUBLDR) +714bps and low income discretionary (GSXULOWD) +487bps.
In Europe, Banks (SX7P) rose 4.3% and EU Renewables (GSXERNEW) rose 1.2%, while Defence (GSSBDEFE) fell 1.8%.

Historical stat: since 1952 the 12 months after a midterm have been the strongest stretch of the four-year cycle for the S&P 500. Across 18 midterms the index averaged +7.5% through year end, +13.9% over the next 6 months and +15.5% over 12 months, and was higher at both the 6 and 12 month marks in all 18 instances.

Thematics: 21 US baskets had a move of more than 3 sigma yesterday, the 2nd highest on a 1 year lookback (the 5th of June was 25). Markets are focused on less data center, less defense budget, more homebuilding and more healthcare subsidies.
Basket moves: ACA Beneficiaries (GSHLCACA) +9%, Homebuilders (GSXUBLDR) +7%, Hyperscalers (GSXUHYPR) +4%, NeoClouds (GSXUNEOC) -8%, Power Up (GSENEPOW) -6%, Defense Spending (GSXUDFNS) -5%.
Rheinmetall (Buy, PT EUR2100, 100% upside): operating profit ahead but revenue softer, and FY26 sales and operating margin guidance lowered. Free operating cash flow was -€82mn vs consensus +€123mn.

Legrand beat and raised, with organic growth +19% vs consensus +11% and a 10% adjusted EBIT beat. Positioning in electricals has been 'clingy' but length was reduced further yesterday, so a small bounce is possible today.

Maersk initial take looks very weak vs expectations on Q3 EBITDA of $4.7bn vs consensus $5.32bn, despite an upgraded FY26 EBITDA guide to $14-14.5bn that was already priced in by consensus ($14.2bn) and the buyside ($16bn+).

DTE had mixed results: group revenue and EBITDA AL beat and OFCF beat on lower capex, offset by a lower buyback and press reports that TMUS merger aspirations are not over. Germany EBITDA growth is now expected at the low end of the 2.5-3% FY26 guidance.
IMCD Q3 was judged not good enough given the large drop in oil over the past 24 hours: gross profit 2% beat, EBITA in line.
Commerzbank missed expectations and lowered NII guidance: net profit 1% below company consensus and CET1 of 14.2% is 0.2pp below consensus.
Swiss Re had a strong headline beat supported by reserve release and nat cat, while P&C re top line of 4.5bn missed a consensus that had been cut from 5bn.
Lanxess Q3 was in line, with guidance narrowed to the upper end of 450-500m vs consensus of about 490m, helped by a US tariff refund benefit and lower corporate costs.
Positioning is described as light, with a CTA positioning exhibit referenced.

market_movers.rationale: Rheinmetall is on the Conviction List with 100% upside. Q3 operating profit rose 62% to €553mn, 4% ahead of consensus, but revenue of €3.15bn was 3% below consensus and FY26 sales and margin guidance were lowered.
Legrand beat and raised, with organic growth +19% vs consensus +11% and OSG guidance raised to 11-13% from 8-10% (consensus 10%).
Maersk Q3 EBITDA of $4.7bn was below consensus of $5.32bn, and the raised FY26 guide was already in consensus.
Commerzbank net profit was 1% below consensus, NII guidance was lowered and CET1 was 0.2pp below consensus.

sector_views.rationale: The GSXUBLDR basket rose 7% and low income discretionary rose 487bps as yields and oil fell after the midterms.
Neoclouds fell 7-8%, power 6% and semis 2.5% as the market priced less data center build-out.
Defence fell 1.8% in Europe and the US Defense Spending basket fell 5% on expectations of a smaller defense budget.

earnings_insights: Rheinmetall Q3 (reported 11/5): revenue up 32% to €3.15bn, 3% below consensus. Operating profit up 62% to €553mn, 4% ahead of consensus, a 17.5% operating margin. Order intake €2.89bn. Free operating cash flow -€82mn vs consensus +€123mn. FY26 sales and operating margin guidance lowered.

Legrand Q3 (reported): organic growth +19% vs consensus +11%, margins 20bps ahead, adjusted EBIT 10% ahead of consensus. OSG guidance raised to 11-13% (consensus 10%) from 8-10%, margin guidance unchanged.
Maersk Q3 (reported): EBITDA $4.7bn vs consensus $5.32bn. FY26 EBITDA guidance raised to $14-14.5bn from $10.5-12.5bn, versus consensus of $14.2bn, buyside near $16bn+ and GS estimate of $15.6bn.

DTE Q3 (reported): group revenue beat, Germany service revenue 0.4% ahead, EBITDA AL beat with Germany a small miss, OFCF beat on lower capex. FY guidance raised marginally for the US and non-US guidance reiterated. Buyback lower.
IMCD Q3 (reported): gross profit 2% above consensus with gross margin 50bps above, EBITA in line, 9M organic operating EBITA growth +4.6%, FCF +12% y/y.

Commerzbank Q3 (reported): net profit 1% below company consensus on lower revenues (NII 1% below, other income more negative), partly offset by lower operating and credit costs. CET1 14.2% vs consensus 0.2pp higher. NII guidance lowered.
Swiss Re (reported): headline beat helped by reserve release and nat cat. P&C re top line of 4.5bn vs a consensus cut from 5bn in May and 4.88bn a month ago.

Lanxess Q3 (reported): in line, helped by a US tariff refund benefit and lower corporate costs. Guidance narrowed to the upper end of the 450-500m range vs consensus of about 490m, implying Q4 in line. FCF positive in Q3 and guided positive in Q4.
risk_factors: Lower oil prices are pressuring cyclical and chemical earnings backdrops, as with IMCD.
Further unwinds in AI infrastructure builders (neoclouds, power, semis) if data center spending expectations fall.
Reduced defense budget expectations weigh on defense names in the US and Europe.
vol_and_positioning: Positioning in European electricals has been 'clingy' and length was reduced further yesterday, so a small bounce is possible.
The note describes overall positioning as light and includes a CTA positioning exhibit, with no figures in the text.
geopolitical: US midterm elections and the resulting political backdrop are driving expectations of less data center spending, a smaller defense budget, more homebuilding and more healthcare subsidies.
